propositions: Naming the implicit juju-info endpoint on either side of an integrate selects it.
(Implied premise) Without naming it, Juju would otherwise avoid the implicit endpoint, so naming is needed to 'force' it.
correction: Naming the implicit endpoint on either side (for example `app:juju-info`) restricts the candidates so the juju-info pair is chosen; in 4.1 `juju integrate` does not prefer non-implicit endpoints, so when juju-info and another endpoint both match, the command fails as ambiguous instead of silently picking the other endpoint (only bundle verification discards implicit candidates).
note: getCandidateEndpoints (relation.go:3441) filters by endpoint name on a side when given; inferEndpoints (3610-3686) returns AmbiguousRelation on >1 match with no implicit filtering. Implicit discarding exists only in domain/deployment/charm/bundledata.go:1233-1260 (bundle verification).
Heading/lead-in fragment; its content is tested in relation:42.

propositions: Juju (not the charm) assigns the secret its URI on creation.
`9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g` is a valid example of that URI.
correction: Juju assigns the secret a URI whose ID is a 20-character XID such as `9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g`; the URI itself is written `secret:9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g` (or `secret://<model-uuid>/9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g` with the source model).
note: The example matches idSnippet `[0-9a-v]{19}[0g]` and ParseURI accepts the bare ID (scheme defaulted, secret.go:83-84), but URI.String() always renders the `secret:` scheme (secret.go:169-188). The controller allocates URIs with NewURI().WithSource(modelUUID) (domain/secret/service/service.go:87); hook context calls CreateSecretURIs (internal/worker/uniter/runner/context/context.go:942). Code examples use `secret:9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g` (jujuc/secret-get.go:52).

propositions: Every secret operation that identifies a secret accepts its URI.
Labels are accepted only in some contexts, whereas the URI is universal.
note: secret-get and secret-info-get take a URI or --label (secret-get.go:79-87, secret-info-get.go:62-73); secret-set, secret-grant, secret-revoke and secret-remove require a URI parsed by secrets.ParseURI (secret-set.go:71, secret-grant.go:76, secret-revoke.go:79, secret-remove.go:56). 'content' in the claim is presumably a typo for 'context'. Access still depends on ownership/grants.

propositions: A vault secret backend configuration must include `endpoint`.
A vault secret backend configuration must include `token`.
correction: The only mandatory vault backend setting is `endpoint`; `token` is optional in the schema, though in practice you supply it for Juju to authenticate to Vault.
note: endpoint: Mandatory true, Immutable (config.go:30-35); token: Secret but not Mandatory (36-40). ValidateConfig only checks the endpoint parses and client cert/key come in pairs (126-143).

propositions: Any unit (leader or not) can read its own unit databag.
Any unit can read other units' unit databags in the relation.
Any unit (leader or not) can read the application databag(s).
note: relation-get for a non-leader reading its own app (or any other unit) delegates to the controller (jujuc/relation-get.go:241-262), which calls ReadRemoteSettings (api/agent/uniter/relationunit.go:161); readOneRemoteSettings reads unit or application settings with no leader or remote-side check (uniter.go:1998-2016; GetRelationApplicationSettings has none, domain/relation/service/relation.go:1131-1153). Only the leader-local path (ReadLocalApplicationSettings) is leader-gated (uniter.go:1944-1946), and writing the app databag is leader-only. Note: the ops library additionally forbids non-leaders from reading their own app databag; that is a charm-library restriction, not Juju's.

propositions: Production Vault should be configured securely per upstream Vault docs.
correction: Advice about operating Vault itself; nothing in Juju's code confirms or refutes it.

propositions: The kubernetes secret backend's configured token comes from a service account.
That service account needs cluster-scoped RBAC privileges for Juju to operate the backend.
note: Config has a `service-account` key (config.go:22) used by RefreshAuth to mint tokens via CreateToken (provider.go:1330-1349). Juju creates service accounts, roles and role bindings per consumer (provider.go:1109-1121), cluster roles/bindings for the controller model (1124-1136), and CleanupModel always deletes cluster role bindings and cluster roles (113-118), so the account needs cluster-level RBAC rights. Juju does not itself validate the binding up front; failures surface as PermissionDenied (1305-1306).

propositions: Each unit in a relation gets a local copy of all the relation's databags.
correction: During a hook, a unit's context keeps a cache of relation databags that it fills on demand from the controller (its own unit and, for the leader, its application databag are held locally for writing); it does not receive a full copy of every databag up front.
note: NewRelationCache is built with member names only (contextfactory.go:353); Settings/ApplicationSettings read from the controller lazily via ReadRemoteSettings and then cache (cache.go:71-110).

propositions: A Juju secret holds sensitive data (credentials, keys, certificates, etc.) for use by charms.
note: Secrets are key/value content created by charms (secret-add) or users and consumed by charms (secret-get). The definition omits that content is a set of key/value pairs and that users can also create secrets for charms.

propositions: The implicit juju-info endpoint is integrated through the same mechanism as declared endpoints.
note: juju-info is stored as an ordinary charm relation for every charm (state.go:367-373, metadata.go:468-472), so it appears in v_application_endpoint and goes through the same AddRelation/inferEndpoints path (domain/relation/service/relation.go:419-445). See relation:21 for the ambiguity caveat when it is left unnamed.

propositions: Only the leader unit can create an application-owned secret.
The owner can assign a label such as `db-password` when creating it.
note: CreateSecret returns ErrIsNotLeader for application owner when not leader (context.go:926-933); --owner defaults to application (secret-add.go:93); --label sets the label (secret-add.go:91,155-156) and `--label db-password` is the code's own example (secret-add.go:70). Only an empty label is rejected (domain/secret/state/state.go:2109). The leading 'URI vs. label:)' is a heading fragment.
